sentences.text:
By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
252 of 2023 at Police Station Sarsawa, District Saharanpur under Sections 363, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act & 3(2)(5) S.C./S.T.
The applicant is in jail since 31.08.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 16.11.2023.

The following arguments made by Sri Sayeed Saif Ullah, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Shravan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
2. They had eloped together to Haryana.
3. The F.I.R. is a result of the opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.
4. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years of age in the FIR only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.
There is no legal basis for age related entries in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 16 years and 2 months are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statement under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 16 years of age.
(iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is 16 years of age.

(v) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.

sentences.text: 6. The victim and the applicant were intimate and has eloped together.
The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.
7. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant and that she had eloped with him to Haryana.
The victim has asserted that she had consensual physical relations with the applicant.

8. The victim has not made any allegation of abduction, wrongful detention or commission of rape against the applicant in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
9.
The victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has also admitted to accompanying the applicant to Haryana of her own free will.
However, in the latter part of the statement false and aggravated allegations were made to save the failing prosecution case.
10. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
Medical evidence to establish commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
11. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
12. Medical evidence to establish commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
13. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
14. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Jubair be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
